headline: SECOND BEST EVER: Power Metallic Drills 22m at 11.46% CuEq at Nisk Lion Zone — MRE on Track for Q3
snippet: Power Metallic Mines (TSX-V: PNPN) reported its second-best intersection ever at the Lion Zone, Quebec, with hole 26-095 returning 22.00m at 11.46% CuEq including 6.5m at 18.59% CuEq. Grade and thickness are both increasing as the company advances toward its inaugural mineral resource estimate in Q3 2026.

headline: OKO BREAKS 1KM: G2 Goldfields Hits 84.5m at 3.0 g/t Au at Depth — Deposit Still Open as $3B Takeover Closes In
snippet: G2 Goldfields (TSX-V: GTWO) extended its high-grade OKO gold deposit in Guyana to 1,000m depth, with the deepest hole returning 84.5m at 3.0 g/t Au from 915m — including 6.0m at 13.4 g/t Au — and the system remains open at depth. G Mining Ventures (GMIN) has agreed to acquire G2 in an approximately C$3B deal expected to close June 2026.

headline: ACID SHOCK: China's Sulfuric Acid Export Ban Now in Effect — Chilean Copper Mines Holding Under 30 Days of Supply
snippet: China's ban on sulfuric acid exports, triggered by the Iran war's closure of the Strait of Hormuz cutting Middle Eastern sulphur flows, took effect in May and is squeezing copper producers globally. Chile imports over one million tonnes of Chinese acid annually for heap-leach operations; spot acid prices are up 57.9% since February, and some SX-EW copper mines report fewer than 30 days of supply remaining.

headline: Gold Holds $4,565 as Middle East Conflict Keeps Inflation Fears Elevated — J.P. Morgan Eyes $5,000
snippet: Gold traded at $4,565/oz on May 5, up 0.70% on the day, as the now ten-week-old Middle East conflict drives energy prices higher and amplifies inflation expectations. J.P. Morgan and several Wall Street banks have reiterated $5,000/oz targets for 2026, with some forecasting a run toward $6,000.

headline: NGEx Caps Lunahuasi Phase 4 With a BRAND NEW Zone — 34m at 7.25% CuEq, 22,000m Drilled, Phase 5 Planned
snippet: NGEx Minerals (TSX: NGEX) wrapped Phase 4 drilling at its Lunahuasi copper-gold-silver project in Argentina with a new high-grade zone discovered 300m east of the Mars structure, only 60m below surface and open in all directions. The 22,000m program also returned 34m at 7.25% CuEq and 48m at 7.72% CuEq; Phase 5 planning is underway.

headline: U.S. REGULATOR: The Silver Market Is STRUCTURALLY BROKEN — SILVER Act Would Force Vault Diversification Away From NYC
snippet: A U.S. regulator declared at a House Agriculture Committee hearing that the silver market is structurally compromised, citing the near-total concentration of exchange-approved precious metals vaults within 150 miles of New York City. The bipartisan SILVER Act would direct the CFTC to broaden vault access nationally; CFTC Chairman Michael Selig has pledged support.

headline: Who's Winning Junior Mining's 2026 Exploration Race? Africa and Latin America Are the New Frontiers
snippet: A new analysis finds junior miners are shifting exploration capital to Africa, Central Asia, and South America as Western greenfields become harder to find. ESG compliance and satellite-enabled targeting are emerging as key competitive advantages, with investors rewarding data-driven, discovery-stage companies over legacy explorers.

headline: TOXIC SURGE: Myanmar's Unregulated Rare Earth Mining Is Poisoning the Mekong — Millions of Farmers at Risk
snippet: Water samples from tributaries of the Mekong River show high concentrations of dangerous heavy metals from an unregulated rare earth mining boom centered in Myanmar that is spreading into Laos. Rising global demand for rare earths — critical for EV motors, wind turbines, and defense systems — is driving the extraction surge with little regulatory oversight, threatening farms and fisheries that millions depend on.

headline: RARE EARTH PRICES HIT 2-YEAR HIGH as MP Materials Halts China Shipments — Supply Chain Standoff Escalates
snippet: Rare earth prices have surged to a two-year high after U.S. producer MP Materials announced it is halting ore and concentrate shipments to China. The move compounds existing supply chain stress from Chinese export controls and escalates the critical minerals standoff between Washington and Beijing, raising concerns about near-term supply for Western manufacturers.

headline: Core Lithium Boots Up Finniss After Two Years — Open-Pit Mining Begins This Month With Glencore Strategic Partnership
snippet: Core Lithium has commenced open-pit mining at the Grants deposit in Australia's Northern Territory, restarting the Finniss lithium operation after two years in care and maintenance. A A$50M NRW mining contract and a A$290M funding package anchored by a Glencore strategic investment target first spodumene concentrate shipment in Q4 2026.

headline: Uranium Holds $86.45 — Up 23% Year-Over-Year as Kazatomprom Embraces 'Value Over Volume' Output Cuts
snippet: Uranium spot prices held at $86.45/lb as of May 5, a 23% gain year-over-year, with Kazakhstan's Kazatomprom cutting output by roughly 10% for 2026 to prioritize market balance over volume. AI-driven electricity demand, the U.S. DOE's $2.7B domestic enrichment commitment, and Canada's first newly-approved uranium mine in 20 years (Denison's Wheeler River) are underpinning the bull case.

headline: COT Report: Gold and Silver Speculators Hold Elevated Longs — Positioning Signals Near-Term Caution
snippet: The May 1 Commitment of Traders report on gold, silver, and the U.S. Dollar Index shows speculative positioning at historically elevated levels. GoldSeek's weekly COT analysis tracks large-trader and commercial-hedger moves that have historically preceded near-term price corrections in precious metals — important context for retail investors sizing positions at all-time high gold prices.
